tone_statements.citation: Hulstaert, Gustaaf. 1990. Le dialecte des Elembe. Annales Aequatoria 11: 227-250.
tone_statements.quote: 1. PHONOLOGIE A ce sujet il y a peu de choses à remarquer. [...] Tout comme en Nk. le ton d'une voyelle élidée se jette sur la voyelle suivante. Dans ce cas le préfixe £ [ɛ] remplace son ton bas par le ton haut éventuel de la voyelle élidée : la stêko/1'étêko au puits.
tone_statements.translation: 1. Phonology. On this subject there is little to remark. [...] Just as in Nk[undo], the tone of an elided vowel throws itself onto the following vowel. In that case the prefix ɛ replaces its low tone with the high tone, if any, of the elided vowel: la ɛtɛko / l'ɛtɛko 'at the well'.
tone_statements.locator: p. 229 as printed, sec. 1 'Phonologie'; 'Nk.' = base Nkundo dialect

tone_statements.citation: Motingea Mangulu. 1989. Esquisse grammaticale du lonkutsu. Annales Aequatoria 10: 91-116.
tone_statements.quote: Il existe deux tons de base : bas et haut; et deux doubles: montant et descendant. La tonalité respecte l'allure générale du N tant pour les nominaux, les verbaux que pour les pronominaux. Quelques mots invariables étant propres au lonkutsu ont une tonalité particulière. Ajoutons plutSt [plutôt] qu'il a été constaté de légères différences tonales entre Ie pa~Ier [le parler] d'Ok~la [Okála] ett celui de Ohambe [...] Mais en réalité, dans beaucoup de cas il s'agit dans les deux parlers d'un ton pausal, c'est-à-dire qu'à la limite de l'énoncé Ie [le] ton haut est réalisé plus ou moins bas.
tone_statements.translation: There are two basic tones: low and high; and two compound ones: rising and falling. The tonality follows the general pattern of N[kundo] for nominals, verbals and pronominals alike. A few invariable words peculiar to Lonkutsu have a particular tonality. Let us add rather that slight tonal differences have been observed between the Okala variety and that of Ohambe [...] But in reality, in many cases what is involved in both varieties is a pausal tone, i.e. at the utterance boundary the high tone is realised more or less low.
tone_statements.locator: p. 99 as printed, sec. 1.9 'Tonalité'; 'N' = lonkundó (defined p. 92)

tone.says: No tone inventory paragraph; tone is presupposed (all forms tone-marked, H/L as in Nkundo) and the only prosodic rule stated is tonal: the tone of an elided vowel moves onto the following vowel, a low-toned prefix taking over the high of the elided vowel; lexical notes flag nouns as irregular 'sur la base du ton'. Nothing on stress.

tone.says: Two level tones (low, high) plus two compound tones (rising, falling); tonal behaviour of nominals, verbals and pronominals follows Lonkundo (Mongo); slight tonal differences between the Okala and Ohambe varieties, most of which reduce to a 'ton pausal': at utterance end a high tone is realised more or less low. Sec. 1.7 adds that the tone of an elided vowel persists on the following vowel. All data tone-marked. Nothing on stress/accent.

sources.citation: Motingea Mangulu. 1992. Esquisse de trois parlers de la Lokenye (Basho, Woji et Atsulu). Annales Aequatoria 13: 277-414.
sources.note: Nothing on word stress. Atsulu (=Akfudu/Ankucu of Kole, Nkutu proper) 3.1 Phonetique et phonologie p.356-368; 3.1.5 Tonologie p.366-367: tone system as in other Mongo lects; an utterance-final 'ton bas pausal' lowers a final (sometimes penultimate) H, 'simple question de prosodie', tone keeps its distinctive value. Woji 2.1 (p.320-321) and Basho 1.1 (p.280-284): tonology 'n'appelle aucune remarque particuliere'.
